Topic: Geometric Foundations of Linear Algebra: From Systems to Spaces

Target audience: Undergraduate students in STEM

Section: section_1 — Geometric Interpretation of Linear Systems

Lecture lines:
Linear equations define constraints in our spatial world.
Imagine a robot arm constrained by these equations.
The intersection of these constraints identifies a pose.

Planned animations:
Display two vectors originating from the origin in 2D space. (Color: #FF5733)
Animate the vectors spanning a parallelogram to visualize the span. (Color: #33FF57)
Display the linear combination equation: c1*v1 + c2*v2 = b. (Color: #FFFF33)
Highlight the resulting vector b when c1 and c2 change. (Color: #33FFFF)
Rotate the view to show the geometric interpretation clearly. (Color: #FFFFFF)

Section: section_2 — The Inverse Matrix: Unpacking the Transformation

Lecture lines:
Matrices act as transformations on a grid.
The inverse matrix functions as an undo button.
Singular matrices flatten space, losing original information.

Planned animations:
Show a linear transformation map represented by a matrix A. (Color: #FF5733)
Visualize the inverse transformation mapping back to original. (Color: #33FF57)
Display the identity matrix I as the net effect. (Color: #FFFF33)

Section: section_3 — Column Space: The 'Reachable' World

Lecture lines:
Column space represents all reachable transformation outputs.
Visualize this as a span of vector columns.
The cat's reachable movement defines its column space.

Planned animations:
Show the column vectors as directions in space. (Color: #FF5733)
Visualize the span of columns as a 2D plane. (Color: #33FF57)
Indicate a vector b that lies within the plane. (Color: #FFFF33)

Section: section_4 — Null Space: The 'Hidden' Kernel

Lecture lines:
Null space contains vectors mapped to the origin.
These are directions squashed into zero space.
Think of the security camera's hidden line.

Planned animations:
Show a transformation mapping a line to the origin. (Color: #FF5733)
Label the kernel elements clearly near the origin. (Color: #33FF57)
Visualize the null space as a line or plane. (Color: #FFFF33)

Section: section_5 — Synthesizing the Big Picture

Lecture lines:
Invertibility requires a non-empty, unique space solution.
Null space collapsing points prevents perfect reconstruction.
Mapping these spaces defines our full system picture.

Planned animations:
Show the four fundamental subspaces interacting in a diagram. (Color: #FF5733)
Animate the orthogonal relationships between these subspaces. (Color: #33FF57)
Highlight the Rank-Nullity theorem relationship graphically. (Color: #FFFF33)

        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")

        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)

        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom

        return mobject
